title: Financial Inclusion, ICT Diffusion and Poverty Reduction: Evidence from Sub-Sahara African Countries
decision_rationale: Quantitative panel ARDL (PMG/MG/DFE) on 27 SSA economies; exposures are internet and mobile phone penetration; outcome is household consumption per capita used as poverty proxy (families 4 and 5).
exposure_measure: Internet penetration (IP) and mobile phone subscriptions (MP), per 100 people (World Bank WDI); financial inclusion proxied by commercial bank branches per 100,000 adults (COM)

sample.economies_or_groups: 27 sub-Saharan African countries (Appendix 1), chosen on data availability
sample.income_groups_covered: not reported (SSA only; mostly low and lower-middle, some upper-middle e.g. Botswana, Gabon, Mauritius, South Africa, Namibia)

design.estimator: Panel ARDL: pooled mean group (PMG, preferred via Hausman), mean group, dynamic fixed effects
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: Log GDP per capita, inflation; country fixed effects/heterogeneous intercepts

results.indicator: Household final consumption expenditure per capita (poverty proxy) vs internet penetration, PMG long run
results.evidence: Table 3, PMG long run, row IP; text p.147: 'internet penetration reduces poverty in the long run'

results.indicator: Household consumption per capita vs internet penetration, PMG short run
results.evidence: Table 3, PMG short run, row D IP; no stars, yet abstract says significant short-run reduction

results.indicator: Household consumption per capita vs mobile phone penetration, PMG long run
results.evidence: Table 3, PMG long run, row MP; text: 'no impact on poverty reduction both short and long run'

results.indicator: Household consumption per capita vs mobile phone penetration, PMG short run
results.evidence: Table 3, PMG short run, row D MP; printed -3.6605 with SE 0.00178 and no stars, internally implausible (likely typo)

results.indicator: Household consumption per capita vs commercial bank branches (financial inclusion), PMG long run and short run
results.evidence: Table 3, PMG rows COM and D COM; text calls short-run effect negative, contradicting positive printed sign

n_specifications_reported: 3 estimators (PMG, MG, DFE); MG and DFE show no significant ICT effects except DFE MP long run 0.000895**

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language ('exert a significant reduction in poverty'); PMG ARDL with no instruments; reverse causality (consumption driving internet/bank access) not handled; only two controls

exposure_measurement.why: Internet and mobile subscriptions per 100 people are standard; bank branches is a crude financial inclusion proxy

selection_of_countries_years.why: 27 SSA countries picked on data availability; 14 annual obs per country; period inconsistently reported (2004-2016 vs 2017); obs 351 in Table 1 vs 324 in Table 3

outcome_measurement.why: Household final consumption per capita is a living-standard proxy, not a poverty measure; interpretation of positive coefficient as 'poverty reduction' is loose; min value 0 in Table 1 suggests data gaps coded as zero

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: PMG imposes long-run homogeneity with T=14; MG/DFE show different results; unit-root tests report variables I(1) yet no cointegration test beyond ECT; lag selection not reported

selective_reporting.why: Text and abstract contradict Table 3 (short-run COM sign, short-run IP significance); conclusions emphasise PMG significant results only

venue_quality_concern: possible (low-visibility journal with multiple text-table inconsistencies, typographical errors in specification and variable definitions)
notes: Outcome is household consumption per capita (poverty proxy), so classed as family 4 with overlap to family 5. Abstract says IP reduces poverty in the short run but not long run, whereas Table 3 shows IP significant in the long run and not in the short run; conclusion repeats the short-run claim. Text says COM short-run effect is negative but Table 3 shows +0.0191**. Mobile MP short-run coefficient -3.6605 with SE 0.00178 looks like a misprint. Observations 351 (Table 1) vs 324 (Table 3). No instruction-like text found in the paper.
